canonical_definition: Visual Grounding is the ability to link linguistic expressions (e.g., referring expressions, instructions) to specific visual entities, regions, or segments in images (e.g., bounding boxes, pixels) to resolve referential ambiguity and enable task-relevant reasoning. This construct often involves localizing or identifying image content corresponding to textual mentions—such as in REC/REG/GC tasks, grounded VQA, or pixel-level alignment—and may extend to 3D contexts or incorporate visual prompts (e.g., pointers) to enhance precision. While some definitions emphasize reliance on image evidence over language priors (e.g., NaturalBench’s protocol), others highlight its role in reducing ambiguity during multimodal reasoning or its operationalization through contrastive alignment and masking strategies.
